data.name: Albanus
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word 'albus', meaning 'noble' or 'white'. In Christian tradition, Saint Alban is the first recorded British martyr, who hid a fleeing priest and took his place, saving his life but sacrificing his own.

in_hebrew.name: אלבאנוס
in_hebrew.meaning: אלבאנוס הוא שם נוצרי שמשמעותו לבן או שורש לבן
in_hebrew.long_meaning: אלבאנוס הוא שם נוצרי שמקורו בשם הלטיני אלבאנוס, שמשמעותו לבן או שורש לבן. השם אלבאנוס קשור לשם העברי אלב, שמשמעותו שורש או אב. השם אלבאנוס היה נפוץ בכנסייה הנוצרית הקדומה והיה שמו של מספר קדושים ונוצרים בולטים.

in_greek.name: Αλβανος
in_greek.meaning: Αλβανος είναι ένα χριστιανικό όνομα που σημαίνει λευκός ή λευκή ρίζα
in_greek.long_meaning: Αλβανος είναι ένα χριστιανικό όνομα που προέρχεται από το λατινικό όνομα Albanus, που σημαίνει λευκός ή λευκή ρίζα. Το όνομα Αλβανος συνδέεται με το εβραϊκό όνομα אלב, που σημαίνει ρίζα ή πατέρας. Το όνομα Αλβανος ήταν κοινό στην αρχαία χριστιανική εκκλησία και ήταν το όνομα πολλών αγίων και εξέχουσων χριστιανών.

in_latin.name: Albanus
in_latin.meaning: Albanus est nomen christianum quod significat albus vel radix alba
in_latin.long_meaning: Albanus est nomen christianum quod oritur a nomine latino Albanus, quod significat albus vel radix alba. Nomen Albanus coniungitur cum nomine hebraeo אלב, quod significat radix vel pater. Nomen Albanus fuit commune in ecclesia christiana antiqua et fuit nomen plurium sanctorum et christianorum insignium.

in_english.name: Albanus
in_english.meaning: Albanus is a Christian name meaning white or fair root
in_english.long_meaning: Albanus is a Christian name derived from the Latin name Albanus, meaning white or fair root. The name Albanus is connected to the Hebrew root אלב, meaning root or father. Albanus was a common name in the early Christian church and was borne by several saints and notable Christians, symbolizing purity, innocence, and spiritual growth.

saint_reference.note: Saint Alban was a 3rd-century British Christian martyr and saint.

data.cultural_impact: Saint Alban is the patron saint of England and Wales, and his feast day is celebrated on 22nd February. He is remembered for his selflessness and courage in sheltering a persecuted priest during the Roman Empire, which eventually led to his own martyrdom. Alban's story has been an enduring symbol of the strength of the Christian faith in the face of persecution and adversity, inspiring generations of English and Welsh Christians.
data.spiritual_significance: Alban's life story highlights the importance of Christ-like selflessness and love towards one's neighbor. By taking the place of the priest and accepting the persecution that came with the faith, Alban demonstrated the Christian virtues of sacrifice, love, and sacrifice for the greater good. His courage and conviction in the face of persecution serve as a powerful reminder of the strength and enduring power of the Christian faith.

It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Christian names.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named Elizabeth Albanus in New York, United States credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Albanus, which means "Noble, Kind". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Albanus: The name Alban signifies "noble" or "handsome" in Latin. In Christian tradition, St. Alban is the first British martyr, who sheltered a Christian priest and gave his own name and identity to protect him, ultimately sharing his faith and sacrificing his life. The name Albanus honors this act of selfless love and courage.
